You watch destruction emerge from accumulation: nothing visible happens until the threshold breaks, then cracks bloom explosively across the surface.

crackpropagation_ca.qfep_connection: Edge of chaos — the crack threshold is the critical lambda where order (intact material) meets entropy (shattered field). Below threshold: stability. Above: catastrophic branching. The propagation rate tunes how fast the phase transition sweeps through the grid.

All 3 placements (Fractal_Recursion, Corridor_Fractal_Recursion, Hangar_Fractals_Walk, plus the Curation_Bay_fractals_0 / Proto_Fractal_Recursion copies) are BARE tokens with no #key:value, and apply_grid_config now returns on the first line for an empty config, so none of them reaches the new code at all.
dna.was: stair_size, step_count, show_construction and step_delay were all @export, and apply_grid_config() was `pass` - the knobs existed in the inspector and no map token could turn one. The three build phases ran unconditionally, so the @identity's claim that 'handrails and stringers arise as structural necessity from the step geometry' was a sentence no room could test, and the truth line 'a staircase is a cube that learned to subdivide itself along its own diagonal' shipped at exactly one granularity.
dna.note: assembly is cumulative, not exclusive: treads is the bare result of the diagonal cut (n slabs, nothing holding them), steps closes each slice with its riser, stringers adds the two side walls that make it an object rather than a diagram, full adds the rail, posts and balusters. It bites in the silhouette - the handrail is the tallest thing in the frame and the stringers are the widest, so removing them moves the outline, not a detail. step_count is the artifact's own critical_parameter and its argument, x4 either side of the shipped six: 1 is a single block (a stair with no stair in it), 3 coarse, 6 shipped, 12 fine, 24 where the tread is thinner than the rail and the diagonal reads as a ramp again - the discretisation never becoming the thing it approximates. The two are orthogonal: every assembly value reads at every count. NOT `tick` (zeno_staircase's word for the same ladder on a staircase) because zeno pins its rungs to 1/3/9/27/81 and this artifact's shipped default is 6 - taking the word would either move a live placement or make the same rung name a different number on two staircases.

dna.note: hand promotion. depth is the L-system family's word (lsystem_editor, room_grammar, space_filling_curve_gallery) and this file's own - the export was max_depth, the caption already reads 'Depth: %d'. It is NOT `tick`: cantor_set, sierpinski_pyramid and zeno_staircase share tick | once, coarse, fine, dense, limit for a rewrite reapplied to a SET, and their top rung names an idealised limit object you can gesture at. Here the branch is 4-fold, the ring count is (4^d-1)/3 = 1, 5, 21, 85, 341, and `limit` would be 5,461 tori - a capture hazard, not a picture. Taking tick would have meant taking a word without its answers. packing is sierpinski_pyramid's and cantor_set's word and its four values in their order, and the geometry earns it: every child is EXACTLY internally tangent to its parent at any reduction (offset = R(1-r), child radius = rR, so the far edge lands on R), which means the outermost ring is 2.0 across at every rung and the ring count is 4^d at every rung - extent fixed, census fixed, only the claim on the neighbours moving, which is what packing means everywhere else it is used. contact = 0.50 is not a taste: it is the exact reduction at which the two in-plane children become tangent to each other (2*offset = 2*r), and it is also this file's own script default, from before the scene overrode it. ONE THING DIFFERS FROM THE KIN AND IT IS A FACT ABOUT THIS ARTIFACT: the shipped value is `fused`, the TOP rung, one past tangency - sierpinski ships at contact and has a rung above it, this one already ships overlapping, which is exactly where the moire in its own @identity comes from.
dna.pairs: depth=5 x packing=dust is the ONE cell in this sheet that is not a new picture. _draw_circles refuses any radius below 0.01, and at reduction 0.25 the fifth level is 2.0*0.25^4 = 0.0078, so it is culled and depth 5 renders identically to depth 4. Nothing is broken; the recursion has simply run out of visible scale, which is the honest bottom of a self-similar ladder. Every other rung of dust, and every rung of the other three packings, clears the cutoff.
dna.still_note: the tori tumble, so `rotation_speed: 0.0` is declared as a FIXTURE and not as an axis. The outermost ring's rate is rotation_speed*(1 + depth*rotation_per_depth), which means a depth sweep at a fixed settle time would compare five ring-counts at five different tumble PHASES and hand the critic pose difference dressed as axis difference. Frozen, both axes are standing geometry: depth changes the census inside a silhouette that by construction does not move, packing changes whether that census reads as interference, tree or dust.

Removed middles are drawn only when the row they belong to is itself drawn, so the record's extent - and therefore the capture's union AABB - is identical at all three values and the bite measures the drawing and never the camera.
dna.one_scene_many_names: this .tscn is ALSO the body of `fractal_cantor_set` and of `test_scene_3` in this same registry file - the corpus's most common hidden family, found again here. The axes live on the script, so both siblings inherit them the moment they are placed; only this token carries the declaration, and the other two should be checked before either is promoted separately.
dna.still_note: MEASURED, not assumed: the recursion was re-run in Python at every rung. tick is the strong axis - 3 / 7 / 15 / 31 / 63 bars over 2 / 3 / 4 / 5 / 6 rows, so the silhouette changes wholesale and no two rungs come out identical (checked explicitly, because a naive ladder would have made dense and limit the same picture). removal is the thinner measurement: at the default rung it adds 7 volumes totalling 0.563 of drawn length against the 15 survivors' 1.926, so ghost is about 29 percent more drawn material - but at alpha 0.16 and unshaded, so crop-recheck before believing an INERT verdict on it. scar is thinner still, 7 dark rods of 3.3 mm section against a dark background, and is the hardest value in this pair to photograph. At `limit` the narrowest segment is 3.3 mm against a bar section of 15 x 20 mm, which is Cantor dust and deliberately the last rung: the next one would be a picture of the mesh's minimum feature, the same reason cantor_set stopped at five.

dna.default: depth=6, recession=nested - 6 is the number example_8_2_recursion_vr.tscn has always written on the root (the export is renamed from max_depth and the scene line renamed with it, so the value on disk is unchanged), and the six terms are still 1.0, 0.5, 0.25, 0.125, 0.0625 and 0.03125 at the same centre. depth is also the only term in the colour index and the z step, both of which read (depth - d), so iteration 0 is still red at z 0 and iteration 5 still purple at z 0.015. nested is a NO-OP by construction: _seat returns Vector3.ZERO and _drawn_size hands the size straight back, so _draw_recursive_pattern's call reduces to the shipped _create_square(center, size, d), and _frame_bounds returns the shipped initial_size square so the four frame bars land on the same coordinates with the same bar_length. All 5 placements (Fractal_Recursion, Fractals_Necklace, Hangar_Fractals_Walk and the Corridor_Fractal_Recursion and Curation_Bay_fractals_2 curation_station rosters) carry the bare token with no config keys, and GridInteractablesComponent does not even CALL apply_grid_config for a token that carries none - so no placement reaches an assignment, let alone the rebuild.
dna.was: five @export knobs and not one categorical among them: max_depth an int, size_reduction and initial_size floats, show_frame a bool, frame_thickness a size - and apply_grid_config's whole body was `pass`, so the artifact advertised the hook and threw every key away. The @identity's own declared critical_parameter (size_reduction, 'the ratio between parent and child determines whether the nesting feels dense or sparse') was unreachable from any map token, and every placement got the same six squares. The runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS, which was a fact about the KIND of knob, not about the artifact.
dna.finding: THE BRANCHING FACTOR IS ONE, and it is why the ladder is cheap here and why the file's own truth line overstates its case. _draw_recursive_pattern makes exactly ONE recursive call, so this is a tail call - a loop wearing recursion's clothes - and the population at every level is a single square, not a set. Cost per rung is +1 mesh, against Menger's x20 and Sierpinski's x5. The ladder was measured rather than assumed: the walk stops on `d <= 0 or size < 0.01`, so at the shipped initial_size 1.0 and size_reduction 0.5 the terms run 1.0 ... 0.015625 and the eighth, 0.0078125, is culled. SEVEN rungs build and an eighth cannot, which is the example_8_4 fault (a rung that exists in the enum and cannot be drawn) caught before declaring rather than after.
dna.note: recession is what shape the descent takes, and it is the file's own truth line made switchable. 'A square inside a square is not decoration - it is the first evidence that a function can call itself' is a CLAIM about containment, and the artifact could only ever assert it. abreast stages the counterfactual the nesting was built to refuse: the same six terms at the same six sizes laid along X with their bottom edges aligned, succession without containment - which is what a tail call actually costs, since no frame survives inside another. strata stacks them up Y, each term sitting on the one before, oldest at the bottom: deposition rather than containment. collapsed drives the nest to its own limit, every term drawn at the innermost size inside a frame that has not moved. The run in both laid-out values is the SUM OF THE SIZES THE RULE ITSELF PRODUCED - no spacing constant is invented anywhere - and the colours, the alphas, the z step and the term count are identical at all four values, so what changes between the tiles is the arrangement and only the arrangement.
dna.kin: depth is example_8_3_recursion_circles_vr's word, one file along in the same NOC chapter and literally the same algorithm with tori instead of boxes, and through it the L-system family's (lsystem_editor, room_grammar, space_filling_curve_gallery). DELIBERATELY NOT `tick`: cantor_set, sierpinski_pyramid, menger_sponge, cube_subdivision and zeno_staircase share once|coarse|fine|dense|limit for a rule reapplied to a SET, and their top rung gestures at an idealised limit object. 8.3 refused the word because its branch is 4-fold and `limit` would be 5,461 tori; this file refuses it for the opposite reason - the branch is 1-fold, a generation here is a single term, and there is no set to rewrite - and both refusals leave the two halves of one lesson answering to the same word. THE INTEGERS ARE THIS FILE'S OWN and differ from 8.3's 1-5, because its floor is 7 and its shipped rung is 6, not 4. recession is folding_past's word with its four values in its order, and it is already in this file's @identity ('concentric squares receding in Z'). ONE THING DIFFERS AND IT IS A FACT ABOUT THE ARTIFACT: folding_past's abreast equalises the terms' SIZE, because there the rule is about time and the nesting is the only claim; here the halving IS the rule, so abreast withdraws the containment and keeps the halving. Equalising the sizes would have changed the rule instead of the claim.
dna.sweep_note: RUN THIS ONE AT --max=20. build_dna_gallery trims the SECOND axis to fit the cap, and 5 x 4 = 20 against the default 9 trims recession to a single value and drops it, leaving a sheet that measures depth alone and says nothing about the axis that carries the argument.
dna.pairs: AT depth=1 THE FOUR recession VALUES ARE ONE PICTURE, and that is the axis reporting itself honestly rather than a duplicate tile. One term has nothing to be inside, in a row with, or on top of; _seat's `along` resolves to 0.0 for the single square and _frame_bounds returns the same initial_size square, so the whole column is identical by construction. From depth 2 upward every value separates. The other pair to read with care: depth 6 -> 7 is the WEAKEST STEP ON THE LADDER by construction and should not be the pair an INERT verdict is read from. The seventh term is 0.015625 across against a frame 1.06 wide - 1.5% of the picture - so it lands as a handful of pixels at dead centre. It is declared anyway because it is the true floor and because the palette has six colours: at depth 7 the index wraps and the innermost square comes back RED, the labels running out before the recursion does. Every other pair on the ladder (1 vs 2, 2 vs 4, 4 vs 6) changes the square count and the colour census outright.
dna.still_note: the EXTENT MOVES ON recession and the camera is placed once on the union, so read the tiles with that in hand. at the shipped depth 6 and frame_thickness 0.03 the frame measures 1.06 x 1.06 for nested and collapsed, 2.03 x 1.06 for abreast and 1.06 x 2.03 for strata - the run being the sum of the terms, 2 x initial_size x (1 - 0.5^n) = 1.96875, which converges on 2.0. So the union is roughly 2.03 square and the nested tile fills about a quarter of it: well clear of the ~6% floor, but not the full-frame subject a single-value capture would have given. collapsed is the thin tile of the four - an unmoved frame with a 0.03 m multicoloured speck at its centre - and that is the value doing its job, not the bench failing. No fixture is needed: grep the file for randf, randi, noise or a clock and there is nothing, _ready ends on set_process(false), and the drawing is finished before the first frame - so a variant here is a fact and not a sample.
dna.declines: size_reduction, initial_size and frame_thickness stay plain numeric exports, now reachable through apply_grid_config but not declared: a denser nest or a bigger picture is a size change, not a different claim. A `coding` axis over the palette (the six-colour rainbow labels each generation, which is exactly what self-similarity says you cannot do) was considered and left for a later pass - it is real and it is cheap, but it argues about the LEGEND and recession argues about the recursion, and only two axes are swept.

dna.default: tick=coarse, removal=gone - coarse SHORT-CIRCUITS: _levels() hands back the shipped max_iterations rather than the table's 2, so a scene that overrides the count in the inspector is not silently retuned by this promotion. gone draws nothing where the seven cross-cubes were, which is what this file has always done, because the removed positions were simply never built. build_mode stays grow, so the sponge still subdivides once per subdivision_interval second on the same clock. apply_grid_config was a bare `pass` and is now guarded twice - a word is taken only when it validates AND differs, and _rebuild() fires only after _built - so the nine placements pass no key, reach no assignment and never rebuild. THE AXIS DEFAULTS PRESERVE AND THE ARTIFACT DOES NOT: two defects were repaired in this pass and they DO change what those nine maps draw. See `finding`. Both are repairs toward the object this entry, the README, the @identity and the file's own comments have always described, and neither is reachable as an axis value.
dna.finding: TWO DEFECTS, both older than this promotion, both repaired here. (1) THIS WAS NOT A MENGER SPONGE. `var z = i / 9.0` is a FLOAT divide, so the z layer index of the 3x3x3 lattice came back as 0, 1/9, 2/9 ... 26/9 instead of 0, 1, 2. The twenty kept sub-cubes were smeared along z at ninth-of-a-cell offsets and ran from z=-3 to z=+5.67 against a parent spanning -4.5 to +4.5 - which is why this entry's own footprint reads 10 deep on a 9 m cube. x and y were computed correctly and the keep_positions table is correct (it removes exactly {4,10,12,13,14,16,22}, the six face centres and the body centre), so the entire fault was one character, and the three orthogonal corridors the @identity promises never existed. The fix makes the object SMALLER in z and never larger, so no placement can gain a collision from it. (2) IT ATE ITS NEIGHBOURS. find_all_cube_scenes() walked get_tree().current_scene - the whole map - and matched any node named CubeScene* or InitialCube or instanced from cube_scene.tscn. GridSystem.gd holds exactly such a node at $CubeScene (line 69), hides it, duplicates it to build the floor and re-acquires it BY NAME on reload; a dozen other artifacts are built from the same primitive, cube_subdivision and sierpinski_pyramid among them. Every one of those was subdivided into twenty pieces and the original freed, once per second, in any map holding this token. The walk now starts at `self`.
dna.was: three @export knobs and not one categorical among them: subdivision_interval is a duration, max_iterations a count, auto_start a flag - and apply_grid_config's whole body was `pass`, so max_iterations, which the @identity names as this artifact's critical_parameter, was unreachable from any map token. Every placement got two iterations on a one-second clock. The runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS, which was a fact about the KIND of knob, not about the artifact.
dna.kin: tick is cantor_set's and sierpinski_pyramid's word, and once | coarse | fine are the first three of their five value names character for character. THE LADDER STOPS AT THREE AND THE SHORTNESS IS THIS ARTIFACT'S OWN ARGUMENT, not drift in the word: every Menger tick multiplies the cube count by TWENTY, so the rungs are 20, 400 and 8000 cube_scene instances and a fourth would be 160,000, each carrying a StaticBody3D and a CollisionShape3D. Cantor reaches five rungs at 32 bars because its rule multiplies by 2, and Sierpinski at 3125 because its multiplies by 5. D = log(20)/log(3) = 2.727 is exactly why this ladder is short, so declaring dense and limit would be the example_8_4 fault - rungs that exist in the enum and cannot be built. The shipped value sits in the MIDDLE of what remains, so this ladder runs both ways. removal is cantor_set's word with its three values, its ghost colour, its 0.16 alpha, its unshaded flag and its 0.22 scar ratio lifted unchanged, so the 1D and 3D removal fractals photograph alike. sierpinski_pyramid REFUSED this same word and was right to: its five children's bounding volumes interpenetrate and there was no complement to draw. Menger's 27 sub-cubes partition the parent exactly - no overlap, no gap - so here the complement is a real set and ghost can put it back.
dna.note: removal is this artifact's own truth made drawable. 'A solid made entirely of holes' has until now been argued by an object with nothing at all where the holes are. gone is that silence. ghost restores each deleted cross-cube as a pale full-size volume, so the sponge reads as the whole cube with its subtractions marked and the eye can watch volume leave at every scale at once; scar leaves a small dark core at 22 percent of the cell, so the holes read as a lattice of markers rather than as empty air. build_mode is deliberately NOT an axis and is the fixture instead, for cantor_set's reason: the shipped artifact subdivides once per second, so a still taken at boot holds ONE 9 m cube and the whole of tick is invisible to it. `instant` runs the identical subdivide call inside _ready, carrying the frontier list forward explicitly rather than re-scanning, because queue_free does not take effect until the end of the frame and a second scan within one _ready would find the already-subdivided originals again.
dna.still_note: tick is the strong axis: 20 / 400 / 8000 cubes at 3 m, 1 m and 0.333 m inside an unchanged 9 m envelope, so under fit-to-AABB framing the silhouette holds while the texture inside it changes wholesale - which is the point, since self-similarity is exactly the claim that the outline does not change. COST WARNING for whoever runs the sweep: `fine` builds 8000 cube_scene instances, each with a StaticBody3D and a CollisionShape3D, which is 2.5x the frame sierpinski_pyramid already flagged as the one that could trip the 16-second watchdog. It is built inside _ready, so it falls under the 45 s boot grace rather than the 16 s stall timer; if it still trips, the fix is the grace and not a shorter ladder. With removal=ghost that same frame adds 2947 translucent boxes on top of it. removal is the thinner measurement and should be judged at once or coarse before an INERT verdict is believed at fine, where the outer ghosts overlay the inner survivors.
dna.declines: subdivision_interval stays a plain export: a rate is invisible to a still, and it is the thing the fixture exists to step around rather than a thing to declare. auto_start stays a flag - its false value renders as one bare cube, which is half a sheet of near-blank frames for no argument.

mushrooms.qfep_connection: E(S) entropy filtered through ecological form — noise is the raw entropy, density threshold is the filter, and species templates are the forms that entropy fills. Fairy rings are emergent order: lambda-tuning where structured patterns crystallize from random placement.
mushrooms.gamwell_reference: Spatial Poisson processes, noise-driven procedural generation, fairy ring mycology, bioluminescent fungi, ecological niche theory
interactions: find fairy rings — perfect circles of identical species
spot glowing mushrooms in the undergrowth
notice how clearings form from noise thresholds
mushrooms.capacity: EXPLAIN how noise-driven spatial processes create naturalistic distributions and how fairy rings emerge as self-organized order within random fields.

necklace_anchor.description: Pendant necklace display on a stand showing the concept of an identity anchor point. A vertical stand with torus ring, glowing gem pendant that slowly rotates.
necklace_anchor.name: Necklace Anchor

penteract_double_projection.description: 5D hypercube (penteract) projected twice â€” from 5D to 4D to 3D. The shadow of a shadow of a higher-dimensional object, revealing structure invisible from any single viewpoint.
penteract_double_projection.name: Penteract Double Projection
penteract_double_projection.qfep_connection: Thirty-two vertices, an edge wherever two indices differ by one bit, then two flattenings in a row before anything is drawable. What orbits in front of you is a compression of a compression, recomputed every frame — the penteract never arrives, only its loss schedule.

percolationnetwork_ca.description: P(occupied) = threshold -> CA flow propagation from top to bottom — does the random lattice percolate?
percolationnetwork_ca.name: percolationnetwork_ca

dna.default: occupation=conductive (p = 0.40), inlet=face - the shipped constant and the shipped top-face seeding exactly, same materials and same collision rule, so all 5 existing placements are unchanged; no map carries an #occupation: or #inlet: token today
dna.was: zero exports on the one artifact in the corpus whose whole subject is a number. Its own @identity block names PERCOLATION_THRESHOLD as the critical parameter and then lists a threshold control under `needs` as MISSING - the value was a const, so every player who ever met this lattice met p = 0.40, comfortably above the 3D site-percolation point p_c ~= 0.3116. The claim 'below the threshold nothing connects, above it everything does, and at the threshold the system decides' was only ever demonstrated on its winning side.
dna.note: occupation is p, how much lattice there is: sparse 0.20 (well under p_c - isolated pockets, the flow dies near the inlet face), critical 0.31 (at p_c - the incipient cluster, fractal, the outcome genuinely open), conductive 0.40 (the shipped value), dense 0.60 (everything connects and the paths stop being paths), solid 0.80 (a wall; percolation is trivial and the network is no longer one). inlet is the boundary condition - where the flow is injected: face = every open site on the +z face, the shipped rain front; point = the open site nearest that face's centre, so one dendrite grows and the question becomes about ONE cluster instead of all of them; seam = one row, a line source spreading as a sheet; shell = all six faces, flow arriving from outside inward, which asks not whether the lattice spans but whether anything in it stays dry. An inlet only ever marks sites the lattice already opened, so p and the boundary stay independent.
dna.warning: WHITE (occupied) CUBES CARRY COLLISION and the player walks inside this lattice. dense and solid are honest arguments and bad rooms - they are bench values. Nothing above conductive should be placed in a walked map without re-running the pathfinder on it.
dna.fixture_note: the lattice and the flow jitter have always come from the global unseeded randf(), so five variants of an unseeded lattice are five different objects rather than five values of one axis. lattice_seed = -1 preserves the shipped behaviour exactly and is the default; the fixture pins 7 so a sweep measures the axis and not the dice.
dna.reads: this scene's root carries the script, so apply_grid_config arrives directly; it is guarded on change (a rebuild recasts 5,832 cells and their collision bodies, which must not happen because a placement passed an unrelated key). _read_grid_config_meta also reads the config_<key> metadata the grid writes before the scene enters the tree, so a token builds the right lattice once instead of building the default and tearing it down.

percolationnetwork_ca.qfep_connection: Percolation: raise the density of open cells and, at one sharp threshold, disconnected pockets suddenly span the whole space — a path appears from edge to edge where an instant before there was none. The turn's physics: connectivity is not gradual, it is a phase change, and the procedural world snaps from rubble to network at a single critical value. Where forests burn, fluids seep, and rumors spread.

recursive_chair.description: Chair created through recursive cube subdivision
recursive_chair.name: Recursive Chair

dna.default: removal=gone - the eleven deleted subcubes are not drawn, which is what this artifact has always done: _step_1_first_subdivision tagged them "remove" and simply never called _create_cube, and the new else-branch calls _spawn_removed_cell, whose first line returns when removal is "gone". Every kept cube, every deform factor (seat *0.15, legs *0.4/*0.4/*2.5, back *2.0/*0.2), the armrests and the five generation colours are untouched. All four placements (Fractal_Recursion, Proto_Fractal_Recursion, Hangar_Fractals_Walk, and the Corridor_Fractal_Recursion curation station) are bare tokens passing no keys, and apply_grid_config - a bare `pass` before this pass - now rebuilds only when a declared word both validates and DIFFERS, and only after _ready has built once.
dna.was: three exports and not one categorical among them: chair_size is a size, step_delay a duration, show_animation a bool the harness could not set (a typed bool rejects a config string before _ready). The runner refused the token for NO TURNABLE KNOBS, which was true of the KIND of knob. Meanwhile the file's own truth line - 'the chair was always inside the cube, subdivision merely removed what was not chair' - was made by an object that never showed a cube.
dna.note: The word is cantor_set's, character for character, from this same registry file: gone/ghost/scar, and the two material recipes are copied value for value (ghost = unshaded alpha 0.16 at Color(0.86,0.88,0.96); scar = matte Color(0.09,0.09,0.11) at 0.22 of the cell) so the siblings LOOK alike answering it. It fits here for the exact reason sierpinski_pyramid refused it: those children's volumes interpenetrate and have no complement to draw, whereas these 27 cells partition one cube, 16 kept and 11 removed, disjoint by construction. build_mode is the FIXTURE, not an axis - the chair assembles one step every 0.5 s, so a still at the harness's 1.1 s settle catches it at step 2, seatless and legless and one frame from step 3; "instant" runs the same five steps in _ready. SIBLING NOT TOUCHED: recursive_table is a separate script and a separate scene (not a shared generator), and the same word fits it exactly - its own truth line is 'a table is a cube that kept its top layer and four corners, everything else was excess', and its 3x3x2 lattice removes 5 of 18 cells the same way. It is assigned elsewhere in this batch, so it was left alone rather than edited under two hands.

recursive_table.description: table = subdivide_3x2(cube) -> keep(top_layer, corner_legs) -> flatten(top) -> stretch(legs)

dna.default: keep=corners, assembly=full - corners returns the shipped test character for character: _is_leg_cell falls past every match case to `return (x == 0 or x == 2) and (z == 0 or z == 2)`, the four corner cells of the bottom layer and nothing else. The apron SHORT-CIRCUITS with it: leg_inset stays the shipped literal table_size * 0.35 rather than being derived, because the corner legs actually stand at table_size / 3 and deriving would move the apron of the three existing placements by 0.017 * table_size. full is the only assembly this artifact could ever build - all three gate helpers return true, so _build_instant and _execute_step run steps 0-4 in the identical order over the identical geometry. All 3 placements (Fractal_Recursion, Hangar_Fractals_Walk, Proto_Fractal_Recursion, plus the Corridor_Fractal_Recursion curation_station list) are BARE tokens - the ':0:-0.5:0.2' suffix is rotation and offsets, not config keys - and both axes are read only inside `if config.has(...)`, so none of them reaches the new code.
dna.was: three @export knobs and not one categorical among them: table_size is a scale, show_animation a flag, step_delay a duration - and apply_grid_config's whole body was `pass`, so not one of them was reachable from a map token, which is why the stage-2 runner refused this for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The essence line is literally `keep(top_layer, corner_legs)` and the critical_parameter is named as 'the top-layer vs bottom-layer role split', yet that split was four hard-coded corner tests buried in _step_1 - the one choice the artifact declares as its own subject was the one thing no placement could vary. The four steps then ran unconditionally, so the truth line ('everything else was excess') could only be shown as its finished result, with the excess never on view.
dna.shared_with: cube_staircase - `assembly` is that artifact's word, promoted the same week one folder over in the same subdivision family, with its terminal value `full`. The same question (how much of the built object is standing, in cumulative rungs) asked of this object's own parts. The rung NAMES are necessarily this table's, exactly as cube_staircase's treads/steps/stringers are its own; a shared vocabulary that forced a table to have treads would be the folding_past mistake. `keep` is this artifact's own word, taken from its own essence line rather than invented, and deliberately NOT `selection` - that word is already the evolution family's (drift|uniform|culled|runaway|split, four artifacts) and means natural selection.
dna.note: The fixture is load-bearing for the evidence, not decoration. show_animation defaults to true and recursive_table.tscn sets step_delay = 0.5, so the four build steps land at 0.5s, 1.0s, 1.5s and 2.0s - while capture_config_sweep's SETTLE is 1.1s. Swept as shipped, every variant would be photographed half-built at the slab stage, `legs` and `full` would be pixel-identical, and the axis would read INERT as a fact about the capture clock. Setting the flag false takes the instant path, so each frame shows the rung it names. It is a real JSON boolean, not the string "true" that a typed bool export rejects before _ready.

romanesco.description: romanesco(cone, depth) = 13 * romanesco(cone * 0.382, depth+1) placed at 137.508 degree golden angle intervals
romanesco.name: romanesco

dna.default: grammar=organic, depth=5 - a no-op on both. organic returns the shipped direction rule verbatim (prefer the longer axis at a 1.3 tolerance, _rng.randf() > 0.5 when near square) and the shipped position rule verbatim (lo + _rng.randi_range(0, hi - lo)), so the RNG is consumed in the same order and the same amount and seed 73 draws the same partition it always drew; depth is the old split_depth export under the family's word, and 5 is the number it shipped with. None of the 8 placements passes a config dict at all - they are bare tokens or rotation/offset shorthand, which the grid routes to overrides and not to config_data - so _apply_artifact_config is never even called for them. apply_grid_config now regenerates only when a value actually DIFFERS and only after _ready has built once.
dna.was: no axis. The registry called this a shape grammar and the grammar was not a parameter: the split rule lived as three unnamed decisions inside _bsp_split (prefer the longer axis, 1.3 tolerance, cut anywhere in the legal band), and split_depth was a plain int export with no config key the map layer routes. The only thing about a shape grammar that was ever variable was the seed - which changes the sample, not the rule.
dna.note: hand promotion 2026-08-03, refused by the runner for NO TURNABLE KNOBS. The four new productions were written against the partition this file already draws (min_room_size still binds, walls and doors and the area-tint are untouched) and each argues a different BUILDING: alternating cuts strictly by recursion level, the textbook BSP, and comes out as nested bands; symmetric bisects the legal band and comes out equal-roomed, a barracks; golden cuts at 0.382 and comes out proportioned, a villa; corridor cuts hard against the minimum, shaving one min_room_size cell off every division, so the plan reads as a spine with cells hanging off it. Three of the five consume no RNG for the cut position, which is correct - a deterministic production is a fact rather than a sample. THE DEPTH LADDER WAS CHECKED, NOT ASSUMED: the partition was re-implemented in Python and run 400 times per rung, giving mean leaf counts 2.00 / 3.75 / 6.81 / 11.25 / 16.56 for depth 1..5 and zero identical partitions between adjacent rungs, so the ladder does not saturate against min_room_size before it runs out. Declared 1-5 and not 1-6 because 5 is the shipped value and the top of the @export_range. SEED IS DELIBERATELY NOT AN AXIS: a seed ladder is five samples of one rule, which is the picture this artifact already had and the reason it read as un-promoted.
dna.kin: lsystem_dungeon.grammar (warren|spiral|branch|meander) and lsystem_dungeon.depth (1-4) ask exactly these two questions of the other top-down plan generator in the corpus, and both WORDS are taken from there unchanged - which production is run, and how many times. The VALUE lists are not shared and must not be: lsystem_dungeon rewrites a string and its four values name turtle topologies, while this file recursively divides a rectangle and its five name where the knife goes. Calling a BSP production 'meander' would make two artifacts look like siblings that measure alike when the only thing they share is that the result is a floor plan. space_filling_curve_gallery.depth names its rungs (sketch|sparse|standard|fine) because it samples one fixed curve; here, as in lsystem_dungeon, the honest unit is the cut itself, so the rungs are integers.

room_grammar.name: Room Grammar

sierpinski_triangle.name: sierpinski_triangle

slime_mold.description: Interactive slime mold simulation using Dave Stewart's tube algorithm
slime_mold.name: Slime Mold
slime_mold.qfep_connection: Pools as nodes, tubes as commitments, a viscosity float doing the deciding: infrastructure without an engineer, after Physarum. But the network is sculpted, not grown — a still life of an optimization, holding the pose of intelligence the organism actually performs.

space_colonization_algorithm.description: Growth algorithm that builds branching structures by attracting tips toward a cloud of auxin-like markers — Runions-style space colonisation producing tree/coral/blood-vessel topologies.
space_colonization_algorithm.name: space_colonization_algorithm
space_colonization_algorithm.qfep_connection: The algorithm that grows a tree the way a tree grows: scatter invisible attractors (auxin, the growth hormone), and let branch tips crawl toward the nearest ones, consuming them as they arrive. No blueprint of the tree exists anywhere — the form is the negotiation between hungry tips and a cloud of demand. Venation, antlers, river deltas, lightning: all this one rule, met with different clouds.

spherenetwork.name: spherenetwork
spherenetwork.qfep_connection: Habitable space made purely by subtraction: CSG carves walkway bores out of solid spheres and the pipes between them, so everywhere you could stand is exactly where material was revoked. Architecture as negative accounting — the corridor is the deficit.

stochastic_tree_separated.name: stochastic_tree_separated
stochastic_tree_separated.qfep_connection: The stochastic tree with its variation pulled apart for inspection — rule and randomness shown as separable ingredients, so the eye can credit each with what it actually contributes.

terrain_erosion.description: Hydraulic erosion on a procedural heightmap â€” layered sin-wave terrain eroded by 800 virtual water droplets flowing downhill, carrying and depositing sediment. ImmediateMesh surface colored by altitude: water, beach, grass, rock, snow.
terrain_erosion.name: Terrain Erosion
terrain_erosion.qfep_connection: Eight hundred droplets rewrite a heightmap that admits, in its own comment, to being layered sines impersonating Perlin — and the RNG is pinned to seed 42, so every visitor inherits the identical island with the identical scars. Erosion as history, but a history that already happened, once, for everyone.

tesseract_net_space_showcase.name: tesseract_net_space_showcase
tesseract_net_space_showcase.qfep_connection: A tesseract can only visit 3-space unfolded, so the room is bricked from its nets — Dalí crosses rotated and offset like masonry, the center deliberately left hollow. You stand inside an absence framed by flattened higher dimension; the fourth axis appears only as the fold that never happens.

tesseract_tunnel.description: Fly through a tunnel of rotating tesseracts â€” 4D hypercubes projected into 3D, their inner and outer cubes visible simultaneously. Experience the shadow of a higher dimension.
tesseract_tunnel.name: Tesseract Tunnel

test_scene_5.name: test
test_scene_5.qfep_connection: The description still reads 'this is the test' while the scene grows the finished recursive tree. Scaffolding promoted to content without renaming: place the token in a map and a whole tree rises under a label that confesses it was never meant to stay — the registry's dark spot, walkable.

tile_patterns.description: Procedural tile pattern generation and tiling algorithms
tile_patterns.name: Tile Patterns

torso_estimation_vis.description: 3-point torso estimation demo — shows how head + two hand positions estimate torso orientation. Animated tracking points with visible shoulder computation and forward direction.
torso_estimation_vis.name: Torso Estimation Visualization

tree_gen.description: An infinite procedural forest that grows around you. Trees spawn within a generation radius as you walk, and vanish behind you when you leave. The generation loop is the algorithm: proximity check, spacing constraint, spawn, cull. No tree exists until you approach; the forest is an illusion maintained by continuous generation. Two tree styles (simple blocks and complex clusters) with red emissive materials create an alien forest that feels both procedural and alive.
tree_gen.name: Tree Generator
tree_gen.qfep_connection: Pure phi — the rate of change IS the content. The forest exists only as a process of generation and removal. Stop walking and the forest freezes. The generation_distance parameter controls how far ahead reality extends.
tree_gen.gamwell_reference: Procedural world generation, infinite terrain, proximity-based LOD, parametric tree generation, spatial hashing
interactions: walk forward to generate new trees ahead
look behind to see trees vanishing at removal distance
observe two tree styles appearing randomly
tree_gen.capacity: BUILD a proximity-based procedural spawning system that creates and destroys content around the player position to simulate infinite generated worlds.

truchettiles.name: truchettiles
truchettiles.qfep_connection: One floor cut into four quadrants, each running a different fragment shader — quarter-arcs, diagonal split, dots, zigzag — with a sample solid hovering above wearing the same program. The quarter-arc corner states the Truchet bargain plainly: a single tile plus one orientation bit per cell is enough to produce unbounded corridor, pattern as the cheapest possible seed.

voronoi_diagrams.description: Spatial partitioning using Voronoi tessellation algorithms
voronoi_diagrams.name: Voronoi Diagrams
voronoi_diagrams.qfep_connection: The seeds are real but the instruments are theatre: uniformity_score is elapsed time times 0.85, coverage times 0.9, climbing regardless of what the cells do. A lesson in partitioning space wearing a scoreboard that measures nothing but duration.

water_flowers.description: Floating flowers on physically simulated Gerstner waves — buoyancy, wave alignment, and drift create a mesmerizing water garden. Configurable flower count, water size, wave strength, and drift speed.
water_flowers.name: Water Flowers

wave_function_collapse.description: Procedural generation using wave function collapse algorithm
wave_function_collapse.name: Wave Function Collapse
wave_function_collapse.qfep_connection: Each cell wears its entropy as a floating number and its possible futures as mini-tiles, and collapse always picks on whoever has the fewest options left. Certainty spreads not by decree but by neighbors deleting each other's possibilities — constraint propagation slowed to watching speed.

waves.name: waves
waves.qfep_connection: Water as the sum of its tells: noise textures for swell, a normal map for glitter, Beer's-law fade for depth, edge foam for shore — four quads, none of them wet. Convincingness assembled from parts, each shader a different bet on which cue the body will believe.

wfc.description: Wave Function Collapse algorithm â€” generating complex patterns from local adjacency constraints. Start with superposition of all possibilities, observe one tile, propagate constraints until the world resolves.
wfc.name: Wave Function Collapse
wfc.qfep_connection: Every cell begins holding all tiles at once, and the world exists only as options are deleted — collapse leaves a single survivor and propagation prunes the neighbours. Compatibility is nothing deeper than one edge-string equalling another reversed: global coherence rented entirely from local string-matching.

rd_coral_garden.name: Gray-Scott Coral Garden
rd_coral_garden.description: Walkable polyp forest grown from Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion. Two constants (F, K) — no designer placed the pillars, the rule did. Uses the commons/rd_grammar substrate from the DNA research loop.

gray_scott_comparison.name: Gray-Scott Comparison Garden
gray_scott_comparison.description: Nine mini-gardens arranged 3×3, each running the same reaction-diffusion equations with a different (F, K) preset. Walking between them teaches the thesis directly: same equations, different constants, different ecology. The pedagogical punchline of pattern formation.

seed_orb.name: Seed Orb
seed_orb.description: The new λ_edge affordance for proceduralgeneration. Player throws a glowing seed; where it lands, procedural growth happens around it. Terrain bumps, tile constraints, L-system-like branches. The seed is input, the world is output — an author isn't needed for a world.

registry_info.description: Additional procedural generation artifacts â€” wave function collapse, higher-dimensional polytopes, reaction diffusion, and maze generation. The constructive side of algorithms.
registry_info.name: procgen_extra
